- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model often overestimates momentum; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of early momentum to forecast to capture short-term reversal.
- If model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon (e.g., avg error < -3%), apply a 2–3% upward bias to next forecast, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overestimates upside; reduce forecast by 2–4% to reflect sentiment mismatch.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows mean reversion (price returns to 14–18-day moving avg), model often fails to recognize it; add a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast curve.
